thesis: BHP's FY2026 results (attributable profit $9.8B vs $9.0B prior year, underlying EPS $2.60 vs $2.00, dividend raised to $1.72 from $1.10) combined with a rebound in copper and iron ore prices drove a volume-spike +3.25% gain on Sep 30, with copper now over 54% of group EBITDA versus a historically iron-ore-driven mix. This suggests a structurally improving, more diversified earnings base beyond the pure iron-ore cycle, even though Port Hedland union negotiations remain unresolved and a fatal accident briefly suspended the Escondida copper mine -- live operational and labor risks that management's update only partially eased.
invalidation: A stalled or failed Port Hedland labor resolution triggering production disruption, or a renewed drop in copper/iron ore prices reversing the earnings tailwind, would invalidate this thesis.

thesis: Novo Nordisk's Sep 21, 2026 unveiling of a post-Wegovy growth strategy drew a further share slide, compounding a year of guidance cuts driven by the Trump-administration Most Favored Nation pricing deal (slashing US Wegovy/Ozempic prices), share loss to compounding pharmacies and Eli Lilly, and semaglutide's 2032 patent cliff -- together explaining the stock's ~18.65% 60-day decline. This suggests the pricing reset is still working through the model rather than complete, even though the new growth strategy is management's own attempt to reassure investors that post-patent diversification is underway.
invalidation: A stabilization or beat in the next quarterly pricing/volume trends, or clear early traction on the new post-Wegovy growth pipeline, would invalidate this avoid call.

thesis: ASML's Q2 2026 results beat estimates (EUR 9.33B sales) and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to EUR 43-45B (from EUR 36-40B prior) with gross margin guided to 54-56%, a confirmed, disclosed catalyst explaining the +11.68% 60-day gain as AI-driven fab capex remains the core demand driver. This still supports holding even though a fresh US Commerce Department scrutiny into an alleged China EUV shipment breach (which ASML denies) is an open, unresolved probe with no scheduled ruling date, and roughly 20% of 2026 revenue is China-exposed. The next earnings report (Oct 14, 2026) is a pending binary catalyst that could move the read before it lands.
invalidation: A confirmed export-control violation finding, a walked-back 2026 guidance at the Oct 14 print, or a slowdown in AI-capex-driven orders would invalidate this.

thesis: TMO touched a fresh 52-week high ($682.98 on Sep 24) and is up ~18.39% over 60 days, driven by a run of analyst upgrades (UBS to Buy, HSBC to Strong Buy) projecting a return to 5-6% organic growth by 2027, alongside disclosed margin expansion (adjusted operating margin to 22.8% from 21.9%). This still supports holding, though the move leans heavily on analyst re-rating rather than one single dominant confirmed catalyst, and no new company-specific negative developments (litigation, dilution, leadership change) surfaced in this run's research -- the one prior litigation matter found (a Tennessee jury trial) was already resolved in June/July 2026, before this cycle.
invalidation: A guidance cut, an organic-growth miss versus the 5-6% 2027 target analysts are now pricing in, or a reversal of the recent analyst upgrades would invalidate this.

thesis: Lumentum is up ~24.82% over 60 days on a confirmed fiscal Q4 beat (revenue +110% YoY to $1.01B, adjusted gross margin to 50.4%) and continued execution on its NVIDIA-backed ($2B investment) AI-optics buildout, reinforced by a well-received product showcase at the ECOC 2026 conference. This still supports holding even though the stock's 452% one-year run and an open, unresolved BIS/DOJ export-control inquiry (voluntarily disclosed by the company, no scheduled outcome date) leave it vulnerable to a sharp pullback on any AI-capex-cycle wobble.
invalidation: A slowdown in AI datacenter optics orders, an adverse resolution of the BIS/DOJ inquiry, or a guidance miss at the next earnings report would invalidate this.

thesis: Carvana shares are volatile and roughly flat over 60 days (+3.80%), swinging from a 7.1% drop (Sep 28) to a 6.75% rebound (Sep 29) after Jefferies reaffirmed a Buy rating citing September unit sales running ~40% above Street estimates and ~39% YoY projected Q3 unit growth. This is offset by the ongoing securities class action (In re Carvana Co Securities Litigation) with dispositive motions due Nov 4, 2026, plus separate securities-fraud investigations opened after the January 2026 Gotham City Research report alleging undisclosed related-party dealings with Bridgecrest/DriveTime/GoFi. The operating momentum is real but doesn't resolve the litigation overhang, so the evidence here is mixed rather than a clean read.
invalidation: An adverse ruling or expanded findings in the securities litigation, or a reversal of the September unit-sales momentum, would invalidate this hold; a dismissal of the securities claims or continued unit-growth beats would strengthen it.
